Profit climbed against the same period a year earlier, managed revenue grew at a healthy pace, and every major operating segment posted stronger earnings. Yet the line that drew the most attention from analysts was not about growth at all. It was the decision to dial back share retirements, a move that the company framed as a deliberate ordering of priorities rather than any sign of stress. That tension is what makes the release worth studying. Readers following financial stocks will recognise this as a recurring debate: whether the largest lenders are better judged by earnings momentum or by what they choose to do with the cash those earnings generate. It is an informational review of posted facts and management commentary, not a forecast and not guidance for any capital spending decision. The bank posted net income that rose from the comparable quarter a year earlier, with earnings per share moving higher by a similar proportion. Posted results carried the weight of a loss on capital spending securities, and management also presented a figure that excludes it, which showed even stronger underlying earnings. Managed revenue grew at a solid clip, reflecting broad contributions rather than a single standout line. Net interest income, the spread between what the bank earns on loans and securities and what it pays on deposits, expanded at a pace noticeably faster than overall revenue. Excluding the markets business, which carries its own volatile interest component, the core measure still grew, helped by higher deposit balances, expanding card balances and larger wholesale loan books. The consumer arm posted higher net income on revenue growth that reflected both card and deposit strength. Card services and auto lending was the fastest-growing component, supported by higher balances and spending, while the banking and wealth management line grew more modestly. The bank also noted the addition of a large number of net new checking accounts, a metric market participants watch because primary-account relationships tend to be sticky and cheap sources of funding. Consumer credit remained a point of attention across the industry, and this release offered some reassurance. Net charge-offs, the debts the bank has written off as uncollectible, declined from the prior year even as the provision for credit losses included a reserve build. The largest single profit contributor was the commercial and capital spending bank, which posted net income growth well ahead of the consumer arm. Markets revenue rose solidly, with equity markets posting a particularly sharp advance as client activity and financing demand remained elevated. Fixed income was steadier. Capital spending banking fees also improved, consistent with a healthier environment for underwriting and advisory work. Payments revenue, often overlooked in discussions of the financial sector activity, grew at a similar pace to capital spending banking fees. This is a fee-and-float business tied to the movement of money for corporate clients, and it provides a counterweight to the cyclicality of deals and trading. The asset and wealth management segment grew revenue and profit at healthy rates, with assets under management reaching a record level and client net inflows remaining strong. Inflows matter more than market appreciation in assessing franchise health, because appreciation can disappear in a downturn while inflows signal that clients are choosing to place additional capital with the firm. The company fees on those assets are recurring, which gives the segment an earnings quality that market participants often reward with greater patience. A reserve build is not automatically a warning. When loan books grow, accounting rules require the bank to set aside more for expected future losses on the new balances. Moves of this kind are often read against the wider S&P 500. The reduction in share retirements was the most debated element of the release. Dividends continued to be paid at a substantial level, but net share retirements fell sharply compared with the pace of recent periods. The company said the firm follows a consistent hierarchy of uses for capital: first commit capital in the business and support clients, then pay dividends, and only then return remaining surplus through share retirements. Dimon indicated that the firm believes it can deploy capital over time at very attractive returns, which implies a willingness to keep flexibility rather than retire shares at current valuations. Posted earnings were reduced by a loss on capital spending securities, a portfolio the bank uses to manage interest-rate exposure and liquidity. The company showed results both with and without the item, which is common practice, and the adjusted figure was meaningfully higher than the posted one. The existence of such a loss in an otherwise strong quarter highlights how balance-sheet positioning can affect results independently of operating performance. Securities portfolios gain or lose value as market yields move, and repositioning to improve future income can crystallise losses today in exchange for better earnings later. Readers are better served treating adjusted figures with appropriate scepticism, since they are management-defined, but the underlying point is straightforward. Such language is characteristic of the bank's leadership and is best read as a statement of posture rather than prediction. It explains the reserve building, the capital retention and the emphasis on diversified earnings. A bank that expects benign conditions behaves differently from one that sees a fat tail of adverse scenarios, and the actions here match the second description. For readers, the practical takeaway is that strong posted results coexist with management unease about the environment. JPMorgan operates in a sector where regulatory capital rules, stress tests and supervisory expectations shape how much surplus a bank can return. Ongoing discussions about how capital requirements for the largest institutions will evolve influence the company's willingness to keep extra buffers. Retaining flexibility today may be partly a hedge against rules that change the calculation tomorrow. Another consideration is how much of the quarter's momentum reflects favourable timing. Client activity in equities and financing was robust, deal markets reopened, and consumers kept spending. Each of those tailwinds can fade, and the company's cautious language hints at awareness that a run of strong quarters is not a permanent condition. Competition is also intensifying in payments, wealth and card lending, where both traditional peers and financial technology firms vie for relationships. title: HSBC, JPM, 3 other G-SIBs set up GL1 non profit to further tokenization standards - Ledger Insights
content: Five systemically important banks have set up a non profit, the Global Layer One Organisation (GL1 Org), to develop common frameworks for tokenized financial markets and push for their adoption. The founders are HSBC, Kinexys by JP Morgan, MUFG, Societe Generale FORGE and Standard Chartered, and they are inviting others to join, including market infrastructures, fintechs and policymakers. The move transitions GL1 from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to the industry. MAS launched GL1 three years ago under Project Guardian with a bold ambition, a shared open distributed ledger for regulated finance, sometimes described as a global unified ledger. That didn’t happen. Sources told Ledger Insights the founders were uncomfortable about relinquishing intellectual property rights. So the project settled for something more modest, agreeing on rules rather than building the rails. The result was two toolkits published last year. One is a checklist for assessing whether a network is fit to engage with. The other covers programmable compliance, embedding regulatory requirements into the infrastructure itself rather than bolting them on afterwards. That type of relative strength could make JPMorgan stock an attractive candidate for a bull put spread trade. As a reminder, a bull put spread is a defined-risk strategy, so you always know the worst-case scenario in advance. This type of trade will profit if JPMorgan stock trades sideways or higher, and sometimes slightly lower. This trade offers flexibility in uncertain markets. The strategy involves simultaneously selling a higher strike put option while buying a lower strike put option in the same expiration cycle. In exchange for selling the bull put spread, the trader receives the option premium. The trade has risk equal to the difference in strike prices, less the premium received. Traders who think the bank heavyweight's stock will stay above 330 for the next few weeks could sell a Dec. 18, 330-325 bull put spread for around $0.80. Selling this spread would generate roughly $80 in option premium with a maximum risk of $420. If the spread expires worthless, that would be a 19% return in just over one month, provided JPMorgan stock is above 330 at expiration. The maximum loss would occur if JPMorgan stock closes below 325 on Dec. 18. If that happens, the premium seller would lose $420 on the trade. The break-even point for the trade is 329.20. That's calculated as 330 minus the $0.80 option premium per contract. That's around 6.5% below the current price. Consider setting a stop loss if the stock breaks below 335, or if the spread increases in value from $0.80 to $1.60. Sticking to this stop-loss level will help avoid large losses if the stock starts to decline. title: Astera Labs Has Slumped Since June: Why J.P. Morgan Still Sees 157% Upside - TIKR.com
content: @Cnv Studio from CnvStudio's Images via Canva; @uthfil aziman effendi from Gambar Luthfil aziman effendi via Canva Astera Labs (ALAB) stock is down 19% today, trading at about $181, as chip stocks slid again after a weak outlook from the biggest phone chipmaker and a royalty miss at a chip designer. Astera had no news of its own. The shares are now down 29% in three months and about 63% below their June 30 closing high. J.P. Morgan is sticking with its call. On Nov. 4, the day after the report, analyst Harlan Sur kept his Overweight rating and $465 price target, about 157% above today’s price. Astera fell harder than the market in October’s AI selloff. On Oct. 30, it lost 11% while the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9%, again with no news of its own. Then came the Nov. 3 report. Third-quarter revenue rose 154% from a year earlier to a record $584.9 million, and Scorpio fabric switches became Astera’s largest product family. Management guided fourth-quarter revenue to $730 million to $750 million, well above the roughly $656 million analysts expected. The call took the shine off. When Morgan Stanley’s Joseph Moore asked whether Scorpio X could plateau, CFO Desmond Lynch said “the initial Scorpio X platforms have completed much of their initial deployment ramps.” He still expects Scorpio X to grow through 2027, but I suspect the market heard a yes. A day later, Democrats swept the midterms, and chip stocks fell on fears of tighter rules on AI data centers. Astera closed Nov. 4 at $223.27, down 4.4%, before today’s drop. Sur raised his target to $465 from $280 in August and kept it on Nov. 4, three months into the slide. Most firms went the other way after this report (RBC Capital cut to $400 from $500). On the call, Sur asked about Orion, Astera’s new rack-scale design for enterprise AI, and said “Orion seems to be that sort of perfect solution.” President Sanjay Gajendra put Astera’s content in the first Orion version at about $100,000. See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Astera Labs, along with Wall Street’s revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Astera Labs’ Analyst Ratings Wall Street’s consensus target was $388 on Nov. 2, more than double the $189 of a year earlier. J.P. Morgan’s sits 20% above it. The earnings case holds up. Analysts expect normalized EPS to more than double this year, to $4.03 from $1.84, and to reach $8.19 by 2028. Management guided to $1.62 to $1.66 of fourth-quarter adjusted EPS, against the $1.42 analysts expected, which gives them reason to keep raising. The stock went the other way. Astera traded at 40x forward earnings at the Nov. 2 close, its lowest of the past year, against an average of 72x and a June 30 peak of 143x. At today’s price, it’s about 32x the $5.67 a share analysts expect over the next 12 months. On that same $5.67, J.P. Morgan’s $465 works out to 82x. The fairer test looks a year ahead, when the forward year is mostly 2027. On the $6.50 analysts expect for 2027, $465 is about 72x, right at the one-year average. So the target doesn’t need June’s euphoria back. It needs investors to go from about 32x to 72x, more than double what they pay today, inside 12 months. That’s a lot to ask of a stock this concentrated. title: Democrats to probe JPMorgan's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein when they take Senate control - CNBC
content:
Senate Democrats are gearing up to investigate JPMorgan Chase’s banking relationship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein once they take control of Congress early next year. Democratic staffers on the Senate Finance Committee intend to home in on how high-ranking executives at JPMorgan handled Epstein, a source familiar with the panel’s thinking told CNBC on Thursday. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the probe of the nation’s biggest bank has not been announced. The Finance Committee is likely to be chaired beginning in January by Sen. Ron Wyden, an Oregon Democrat who currently is the panel’s ranking member. Wyden has made clear he plans to make full use of the subpoena powers that committee majorities wield. Democratic staffers aim to focus in particular on decisions about Epstein made by Mary Callahan Erdoes, the CEO of JPMorgan’s asset and wealth management division, the source said. JPMorgan declined to comment. The bank has previously said it regrets any association with Epstein but that it did not assist him in committing crimes. In a 2023 deposition, Erdoes said she was aware as early as 2006 that Epstein was accused of paying cash to have underage girls brought to his home. Epstein had been a client of the bank since 1998. Epstein became a registered sex offender after pleading guilty in 2008 in Florida to a state criminal charge of procuring an underage girl for prostitution. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon in his own, later deposition in 2023, said Erdoes had authority to cut off Epstein as a client. She did not take that step until 2013. Epstein, a former friend of President Donald Trump, ex-President Bill Clinton and many other high-profile people, died in a jailhouse suicide in August 2019, weeks after being arrested on federal child sex trafficking charges. A lawyer for the U.S. Virgin Islands told a federal judge in New York in 2023 that JPMorgan “was a full-service bank for Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking,” and that it waited until after he killed himself to notify the Treasury Department of $1 billion in suspicious transactions related to trafficking by Epstein. “This was a CYA [cover your a--] reporting after 16 years of all of the monies flowing in his JPMorgan accounts after he was dead,” the lawyer, Mimi Liu, said. JPMorgan has blamed former investment banking chief Jes Staley for concealing or failing to report criminal activity related to Epstein, with whom he had a close relationship. Staley, who left JPMorgan in 2013 and later became CEO of Barclays before stepping down in 2021, has denied knowledge of Epstein’s crimes. House Oversight Chair James Comer, R-Ky., after a closed-door interview with Staley in July, said that the former executive had encouraged JPMorgan to keep Epstein as a client. In mid-2023, JPMorgan agreed to a $290 million settlement with victims of Epstein without admitting wrongdoing. That same year, JPMorgan agreed to pay $75 million to settle a separate lawsuit by the U.S. Virgin Islands alleging that the bank facilitated and benefited from the sex trafficking of young women by Epstein. In August, Wyden released a report accusing top officials at multiple banks of “looking the other way” as Epstein moved hundreds of millions of dollars to finance a yearslong sex trafficking operation. “The report exposes how top bankers shielded Epstein from federal scrutiny by delaying the reporting of Epstein’s suspicious financial activity to the U.S. government, likely in violation of federal anti-money-laundering laws,” Wyden’s office said in a statement that month. “It includes new details about the extent of suspicious activity reported by Deutsche Bank after Epstein’s death, new details from bank reports filed about suspicious transfers to Epstein through accounts at Bank of America, and names top officials at JPMorgan Chase and other banks who were responsible for reporting Epstein’s shady activities to the government but instead protected Epstein in order to gain access to Leon Black and other billionaires.” Black, former CEO of Apollo Global Management, was revealed to have paid Epstein $158 million for financial advice in the years after his 2008 conviction. In September, Black sued the House oversight panel, seeking to block subpoenas it had issued him for his testimony and for documents related to its Epstein probe. On Wednesday, Black sued Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., who is poised to become chair of the Oversight Committee in the next Congress, alleging Garcia defamed him in statements regarding Epstein. The lawsuit focuses on Garcia’s claims in a TV interview that Black “is at the center of Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes” and “was one of the last people to actually interact” with Epstein before his death, among others. The Department of Justice’s mountain of files related to Epstein became a major focus in late 2025 and early 2026, after Congress passed a bill ordering the DOJ to make those records public. Trump’s name is referenced thousands of times in the files that have been released. The president has not been charged with any wrongdoing in connection with Epstein, with whom he fell out in the early 2000s. Got a confidential news tip? We want to hear from you. title: J.P. Morgan Snags Merrill Lifer Managing $940 Million in Los Angeles - AdvisorHub
content: J.P. Morgan Wealth Management on Friday hired a Merrill Lynch lifer who managed $940 million in assets in Los Angeles, according to an announcement from the hiring firm. J. Tiffany Yu, who first registered with the thundering herd in 1998, joined an existing team at J.P. Morgan Advisors in Century City, according to the announcement. The team, Elevate Wealth Partners, is led by advisor Eric Gray and includes two other advisors and five support staff. Yu and members of the team did not respond to a request for comment. “Her hire builds on our established presence in the Los Angeles community and strengthens our ability to meet growing client demand there,” Michael Rogers, Los Angeles regional director, said in a statement. J.P. Morgan earlier this year added other advisors in California, including David Amar, who managed $1.1 billion in Los Angeles at William Blair, and Pourya Naeimi, who oversaw $533 million in Palo Alto at Wells Fargo, according to the announcement. They report to Mollie Colavita, a former Merrill Private Wealth manager who took over as head of J.P. Morgan’s wealth unit in September 2025. Naeimi, who joined in September, was one of Colavita’s first hires in the region since taking over. Colavita’s predecessor, Phil Sieg, had set a target in 2021 to more than double the headcount at J.P. Morgan Advisors to around 1,000 from 450. Thanks to its parent bank’s purchase of First Republic’s private wealth unit in 2023, headcount jumped to around 600, although the firm has also suffered some large departures. Last month, two of its top teams, who managed $18.6 billion in assets combined, launched an RIA. Meanwhile, J.P. Morgan also last month hired former Merrill Lynch Private Wealth regional leader Linda A. Patel to be head of its Southeast territory based in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. She also reports to Colavita and succeeds Janet Sweeney, a 40-year industry veteran who retired earlier this year. A Merrill spokesperson also did not respond to a request for comment. The group is anchored by a Merrill team with around $1.8 billion in assets.

Satoshi Nakamoto created Bitcoin in 2009 under a pseudonym. Bitcoin is a decentralized cryptocurrency, not a network operated by a bank or company. Its design supports peer-to-peer transactions without a bank acting as intermediary, while a distributed system maintains the network’s rules. Bitcoin uses proof-of-work mining and the SHA-256 cryptographic algorithm. Those are features of its network, not of the separate Solana token listing. That distinction matters when banks make headlines. A bank discussing custody or an investment product is talking about how clients access or hold Bitcoin; it isn’t changing the underlying network or guaranteeing a price. Bitcoin’s maximum supply is 21 million coins. Programmed halvings, roughly every four years, reduce miner rewards. Both rules are built into the native Bitcoin network. title: US copper pipeline could reach 1.3 million tonnes a year as critical minerals push gathers pace, says JP Morgan - Yahoo Finance UK
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results JPMorgan, the investment bank, says a focus on securing critical minerals supply is reviving US copper investment, lifting its estimate of potential new supply to about 1.3 million tonnes a year. US mined output has fallen about 50% over 30 years to roughly 1 million tonnes, and its share of global mined output has dropped from about 50% in 1900 to below 5%. The bank ranks the US third globally for potential supply additions, behind Chile and Argentina, though most of the capacity is likely to come online only after 2030. Capital intensity is higher in the US, at about $28,000 for each tonne of annual capacity, against a global average of about $26,000. Regulatory reforms such as the FAST-41 legislation are helping to accelerate projects that previously faced lengthy permitting processes, while in-situ leaching and the restarting of older mines are also helping to drive supply growth. Freeport-McMoRan is best positioned in the medium term, with more than 250,000 tonnes a year of potential brownfield growth, albeit at relatively high capital intensity, and JP Morgan rates it 'overweight'. Resolution, the greenfield joint venture between Rio Tinto and BHP, in which they hold stakes of 55% and 45% respectively, accounts for nearly 50% of the US project pipeline, but a final investment decision is unlikely before 2030 given the ongoing permitting and project evaluation process. The US would also need more smelting capacity to process and refine additional copper concentrate domestically, as it faces a primary copper supply deficit of about 1 million tonnes.
